note: Synthetic demo table (I1), deliberately incomplete (I7). Key = drug|<lab><op><value>, lab token lowercase with no spaces (egfr, potassium, alt, ck, ldl). The rule fires on the most recent result for that lab; context_labs adds a trend line (oldest -> latest) to the evidence.

rules.source: FDA lisinopril (Zestril) label, warning on hyperkalemia and renal function monitoring
rules.text: ACE inhibitors such as lisinopril can raise potassium, more so when kidney function is falling. A potassium above 5.0 mmol/L is worth a recheck and a conversation with the prescriber.

rules.source: FDA NSAID class labeling, renal toxicity warning; KDIGO 2024 CKD guideline (avoid prolonged NSAID use at reduced eGFR)
rules.text: Ibuprofen can reduce blood flow to the kidneys, and the risk is higher when eGFR is below 60. Worth asking the pharmacist about other pain-relief options.

rules.source: FDA spironolactone (Aldactone) label, contraindicated with serum potassium above 5.0 mEq/L
rules.text: Spironolactone raises potassium, and its label lists a potassium above 5.0 as a reason not to use it. Worth raising with the prescriber.
